## Ongoing Research

::: {.entry}
**Gender Stereotypes in Social Media Audience Discourse: Evidence from Bangladeshi Artists.** *(Working paper)*

::: {.summary}
Sentiment, keyness, and topic modeling of YouTube comments show that audience gender stereotypes vary systematically across artistic professions.
:::

[Abstract](papers/youtube-gender-stereotypes.qmd){.link}
:::

::: {.entry}
**Bilateral Convergence across the World: Does International Migration Matter?** *(Working paper)*\
[(coauthors: M. Moniruzzaman, S. N. Wadood)]{.who}

::: {.summary}
A country's core or peripheral position in the global migration network, not migration volume alone, shapes whether migration narrows or widens development gaps.
:::

[Abstract](papers/migration-convergence.qmd){.link}
:::

::: {.entry}
**Rethinking the Income-Emissions Relationship: Evidence from Trade-Embodied CO₂ Emissions Networks.** *(Submitted)*

::: {.summary}
Income turning points for emissions shift with a country's network centrality in the trade-embodied carbon network.
:::

[Abstract](papers/income-emissions.qmd){.link} | [Replication](https://github.com/TAD600/Trading_Pollution){.link}
:::

::: {.entry}
**Product Reproducibility and International Trade Patterns: Evidence from Cultural Goods.** *(Under review)*

::: {.summary}
More reproducible products are less sensitive to trade frictions and follow gravity predictions more closely.
:::

[Abstract](papers/cultural-goods-trade.qmd){.link} | [Replication](https://github.com/TAD600/Global_Cultural_Trade_Network){.link}
:::

:::
